subject: Control-plane auth drift during Privanet upgrade — customer bridge and follow-up
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@adeptcare.com>, SRE Team <sre@adeptcare.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-21T09:13:00-07:00
Subject: Control-plane auth drift during Privanet upgrade — immediate bridge

Hi Elena / AdeptCare SRE,

Quick note to confirm: during the Privanet upgrade we pushed at ~08:30 PT this morning you may have seen intermittent control-plane auth failures for ~20–25 minutes. Our on-call flagged a transient token validation mismatch between the management plane and the customer-side agent during a rolling config push.

What we saw: brief 401s on control-plane calls, followed by automatic reconnects. No data plane (inference) requests were dropped, but certain management actions (agent restarts, new model pins) timed out and returned 401/403 for a short window.

Immediate actions taken by Redwood:
- Rolled back the targeted config change at 08:55 PT (rollback id: rb-20280321-3).
- Collected auth logs and session traces; attached a log bundle (privanet-logs-20280321.zip) to this thread.
- Opened a mitigation bridge with Eng and SRE to stabilize sessions.

Next steps we are committing to now:
1) We will run a targeted rollout of a hotfix tonight (ETA 23:00 PT) behind an opt-in canary for AdeptCare only.
2) Provide a short post-incident summary by EOD tomorrow with root cause and action items.
3) Share a draft rollback/runbook we can use for future upgrades (attached).

Marissa is copied to coordinate credits / SLA follow-up and to schedule a technical postmortem call if you want a live walkthrough. Karthik and Aditya are on the bridge and will provide a deeper engineering note.

I’m sorry for the disruption — we know availability during upgrades is critical. Let me know if you’d like us to stop all scheduled upgrades for your Org until we've completed the hotfix and runbook review.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Support Manager, Redwood Inference
soojin@redwood.com

Attachments: privanet-logs-20280321.zip (log bundle, 14MB), privanet-rollback-runbook-draft.md (markdown runbook)

Subject: RE: Control-plane auth drift during Privanet upgrade — immediate bridge

Quick engineering update (notes from the bridge):

Summary: a config key rename slipped through the canary gating logic in our rollout tool. The new key name caused a short-lived token verification path to fall back to an older validator which rejects session tokens issued with the new signing header. The rollback restored the old key name and re-established the canonical validator.

Impact: management API auth failures for ~20m; no inference traffic loss, but management operations (restart, pin, role adjustments) returned 401/403 and timed out.

Action items we are executing now:
- Prepare a hotfix that restores backward-compatible validation for agents <= 1.12.3 (canary tonight).
- Add a preflight validation for key-name changes in the rollout tool.
- Draft a short operational runbook for customers: how to detect this class of auth drift and an emergency rollback command. (runbook attached)

I will attach a short excerpt of the auth stack traces to the internal runbook and post the sanitized logs to the Drive link once scrubbed.

Karthik
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.com

Date: 2028-03-24T15:40:00-07:00
Subject: Post-incident summary and next steps — Privanet control-plane auth drift (Mar 21)

Elena and AdeptCare team,

As promised, here's a concise post-incident summary and the actions Redwood is taking to prevent recurrence. Thank you for your patience during our investigation.

Executive summary:
- Incident window: 2028-03-21 08:33–08:58 PT.
- Primary impact: control-plane management API returned 401/403 for management operations. No user-facing inference requests failed.
- Root cause: rollout tool applied a renamed config key which caused a fallback to an older token validator implementation. That validator rejects tokens with the new signing header format.

What we did:
- Immediate rollback at 08:55 PT restored expected validator behavior.
- Isolated and gathered logs (privanet-logs-20280321.zip) and scrubbed traces to avoid exposing PII.
- Scoped a hotfix to reintroduce backward-compatible validation for agents <= 1.12.3; canary scheduled for 2028-03-24 23:00 PT (AdeptCare only).

Planned preventive work (committed):
1) Tooling: add preflight checks in the rollout service to disallow config key renames without validation and automated compatibility tests. (ETA Q2 2028)
2) Runbook: publish an "auth drift" emergency runbook with single-command rollback and detection scripts. (Deliverable: 2028-04-04)
3) Agent compatibility: expand integration tests for agent versions 1.10.x — 1.13.x and add a compatibility gate in the rollout pipeline. (ETA Q2 2028)

Customer asks we addressed:
- We confirmed the hotfix will not require agent-side changes but will include recommended mitigations you can enable.
- We reviewed your agent version and confirmed AdeptCare (1.12.3) will be covered by the backward-compatible fix.

Operational credits and follow-up:
- Marissa will follow up separately on a one-time credit for the operational disruption and to schedule a postmortem call if you prefer a walkthrough.

Attachments and links:
- Attached: privanet-logs-20280321.zip (redacted logs), privanet-rollback-runbook-draft.md (runbook draft)
- Drive (sanitized traces): https://drive.google.com/open?id=1aBcD_example_doc
- HubSpot: 009763-AC (tracking)

If you'd like a live run-through of the hotfix canary tonight or want us to pause our upgrade window for your Org until you sign off on the runbook, tell us and we'll schedule an immediate call.

Apologies again for the interruption — we're taking multiple steps to make sure rollouts are no-regressions for management operations going forward.

Regards,
Soojin Lee
Support Manager, Redwood Inference
soojin@redwood.com
